guards.what: G1: `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom(base.Owner, list)` (ToyBox.cs:96) is a take-or-skip reward screen for four wax relics; the port grants all four unconditionally
guards.issue:
MECHANISM AUTO-KEEP, one verdict at every site (binding rule 3). RE-VERDICTED from deliberate-divergence to gap by the relic fix pass (2026-07-26); the old rationale's premise -- 'the house rule for NON-CHOICE relic offers' -- is false, because these are choice offers.
THE OFFERS ARE DECLINABLE. `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom` (RewardsCmd.cs:47-50) is `new RewardsSet(player).WithCustomRewards(rewards).Offer()` with no skip suppression, and `grep -rn WithSkippingDisallowed src/` returns exactly TWO lines in the whole source: the definition (RewardsSet.cs:115) and its one caller, NeowsBones.cs:43. Neow's Bones is therefore the ONLY non-declinable relic offer in the game; CallingBell.cs:31, ToyBox.cs:96, SmallCapsule.cs:15, LostCoffer.cs:22, Orrery.cs:27 and GlassEye.cs:32 are plain skippable sets, as is the ordinary combat/boss reward screen that BlackStar.cs:23, LavaRock.cs:61 and WongosMysteryTicket.cs:101 append RelicRewards to.
IT IS NOT AN IDENTICAL OBSERVABLE (binding rule 2), for two independent reasons. (1) A DECLINE IS WRITTEN INTO RUN HISTORY: `RelicReward.OnSkipped` (RelicReward.cs:117-123) does `RelicChoices.Add(new ModelChoiceHistoryEntry(_relic.Id, wasPicked: false))`, and the sim's own conformance runner READS that field (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:429-432), while `sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:435-466 _reconcile_node_relics` is a bespoke replay-time WORKAROUND that deletes relics the sim auto-granted and the save says were not picked. A divergence that needs a workaround is not an identical observable. (2) PICKUP EFFECTS FIRE UNCONDITIONALLY: in C# `AfterObtained` runs inside `RelicReward.OnSelect` (RelicReward.cs:109-115), i.e. only when the player TAKES the relic, whereas the sim's `run.add_relic` fires `after_obtained` at screen-generation time (sts2_rl/run.py:546-553, the call is sts2_rl/run.py:552), so a relic the player would have declined still runs its pickup effect.
STILL deliberate-divergence, and correct: relic/neows_bones G2 (the one `WithSkippingDisallowed` site) and the up-to-N card screens relic/claws and relic/glass_eye, whose purposes `transform_optional` / `card_reward` ARE in sts2_rl/driver.py:77 SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES so the driver really does offer a decline. Agrees with audit/records/event/drowning_beacon.json mechanism EV-4 (gap, 8 event sites). Rule 7: RewardsCmd.cs, RelicReward.cs, RewardsSet.cs, conformance/runner.py, run.py, rewards.py and driver.py are cited here and not all hashed by this record.
AT THIS SITE (LIVE, grade B, escalating to A): ToyBox.cs:87-97 pulls four relics, marks each IsWax and OFFERS them; sts2_rl/relics/toy_box.py:29-35 calls run.add_relic on all four. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py toybox-melt`): a seeded run obtains ['toy_box', 'toxic_egg', 'akabeko', 'potion_belt', 'planisphere'] with the last four is_wax, and potion_belt's after_obtained has ALREADY RUN -- which in the game only happens for a relic the player takes. This is the clearest instance of observable (2) in the mechanism above. It escalates to grade A whenever a pulled wax relic's own AfterObtained consumes an RNG stream (a wax Small Capsule or Calling Bell pulls further relics), which the four-relic pull makes reachable. Toy Box is Ancient and granted by a ported shrine option, so both sides are reachable.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `RelicCmd.Melt` leaves the relic in `Player.Relics` as an inert entry; the port removes it from run.relics entirely
guards.issue: MECHANISM: RelicCmd.Melt (RelicCmd.cs:89-93) is `relic.Owner.MeltRelicInternal(relic); await relic.AfterRemoved();` -- the relic STAYS in the list, and the game stops it working by excluding melted relics from both hook-listener walks (RunState.cs:569 `player2.Relics.Where(r => !r.IsMelted)` for the run-level walk, CombatState.cs:428-435 for the combat walk). Its own doc comment says so: 'A melted relic remains in your inventory, but is unusable.' toy_box.py:41-42 does `run.relics.remove(wax)`, and the sim's Relic base has no is_melted member at all (EXECUTED: `hasattr(Relic, 'is_melted')` is False). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py toybox-melt`): across six combats the sim's relic count goes 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3 where the game's stays 5 for the whole run. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the reason is that every reader already filters): the hook walks exclude melted relics on both sides, so the EFFECTS agree; and every other reader of Player.Relics a ported path reaches filters on IsTradable, which itself excludes melted relics -- RanwidTheElder.cs:74/94 and RelicTrader.cs:79-124/109, mirrored at events/ranwid_the_elder.py:35/51 and events/relic_trader.py:33/38 over the sim's Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:126-136, whose docstring already reasons about exactly this equivalence). The only unfiltered relic-count reader in the whole game source is ILikeShiny.cs:24 (`Relics.Count >= 25`), an achievement badge and out of scope. What would make it live: porting any effect that reads the relic COUNT or the relic LIST without an IsMelted/IsTradable filter, or a conformance check that treats `len(run.relics)` as a parity signal (conformance/runner.py:792 already samples it, to detect newly-granted relics). Filed as a gap and not a waiver because 'nothing ported observes the difference' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Rule 7: RelicCmd.cs, RunState.cs, CombatState.cs, relics/base.py, the two event files and conformance/runner.py are NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N1 (PROMPT.md bug class 13 + the sweep-A pre-diagnosis, SETTLED): `combats_seen` is never reset -- and that is CORRECT
guards.rationale: ToyBox.CombatsSeen is a [SavedProperty] (ToyBox.cs:62-79), i.e. run-scoped and persisted, and the ONLY thing AfterCombatEnd does to it is `CombatsSeen++` (ToyBox.cs:101) -- it is not a reset site. Sim relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to every CombatState, so toy_box.py's instance field is run-scoped too; a relic that melts one wax copy every third combat of the RUN would be broken by a per-combat reset. The pre-diagnosis handed to this batch describes it as 'Sweep A candidate (combats_seen; C# resets at AfterCombatEnd)', which is the PRE-REWRITE sweep-A output -- the override census that sweep-A defect 3 was about. RE-EXECUTED against the CURRENT sweep: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` now prints `toy_box ['combats_seen'] written by: combats_seen<-['__init__','after_combat_end'] C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)`, which agrees with the source. Also faithful: `CombatsSeen % Combats == 0` (ToyBox.cs:102) vs `self.combats_seen % self.COMBATS_PER_MELT != 0` (toy_box.py:39) -- same modulus, and the increment happens BEFORE the test on both sides, so the first melt is at combat 3 and not combat 4 (executed: combats_seen=3 is the first row where the relic count drops).

guards.what: N2 (EXECUTED): `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(base.Owner)` x4 (ToyBox.cs:90-95) and the draws it costs
guards.rationale: The port calls run.pull_relic_from_front() four times (toy_box.py:30-31), which is the sim's transcription of the same factory method including the rarity roll off the player's Rewards stream (run.py:559-589 and its docstring). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py toybox-melt`): the grab bag goes 96 -> 92, so all four pulls are consumed -- the failure mode audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json G2 records (three unconsumed PullNextRelicFromFront draws, `grab bag 96 -> 96`) does NOT occur here. Also faithful: `relicModel.IsWax = true` before the reward is built (ToyBox.cs:93) vs `relic.is_wax = True` before add_relic (toy_box.py:34), and the port's `if relic is None: break` handles the empty-bag case the C# `.ToMutable()` would throw on. Rule 7: run.py and audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the wax-relic search predicate -- `r != null && r.IsWax && !r.IsMelted` (ToyBox.cs:105) vs `r.is_wax` (toy_box.py:41)
guards.rationale: Given G2's deletion, `!r.IsMelted` is automatically satisfied in the sim (a melted relic is gone), and the null check is a C# list-slot artefact. So the two searches pick the same relic in the same order -- the first wax copy in relic-list order, which is pull order -- and the four melts happen in the order the four were obtained. Recorded because the two divergences interlock: a fix for G2 that keeps melted relics in run.relics MUST add the `not r.is_melted` clause here at the same time, or the third combat would melt the same relic forever.
